summary: ANALOCS is a Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) platform and geospatial ranking engine designed to identify optimal terrestrial analog sites for permanent Moon bases and Mars surface missions. By cross-referencing NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) orbital telemetry with Earth observation datasets, ANALOCS ranks field-testing locations in real time based on user-weighted geophysical, thermal, geochemical, and seasonal parameters—helping mission planners avoid poorly timed field campaigns and minimize terrestrial environmental noise.
details:
ANALOCS is an interactive web platform for exploring and comparing lunar and Martian sites with candidate terrestrial analog regions. By integrating topography, environmental variables, and surface composition across reference cycles (30 days for the Moon, 687 days for Mars, and 365 days for Earth), ANALOCS enables researchers and educators to configure variable weights and thresholds to identify ranked analog regions and compatible temporal windows.

How We Addressed This Challenge

  • The Problem: Comparing planetary environments with Earth regions is complex when terrain, composition, and environmental time-series data are fragmented across repositories or cannot be inspected jointly—making it easy to overlook seasonal shifts or terrestrial environmental noise.
  • Our Solution: ANALOCS provides an interactive exploration interface where users select the Moon or Mars, pick a reference site, and configure variable weights and thresholds across topography, environmental conditions, and composition. The platform cross-matches these criteria against an exported dataset of 14 lunar sites, 14 Martian sites, and 1,000 terrestrial regions with daily time series, displaying ranked results, compatible temporal windows, interactive 3D globes, comparative maps, and time-series/calendar charts.
  • Responsible Scope: ANALOCS is designed as an exploratory and comparative analysis tool to support preliminary site triage—not as a substitute for field validation or a guarantee of mission suitability.
  • Tech Stack: Built with React and TypeScript, using Three.js for 3D planetary visualizations and D3 for similarity analytics, calendar views, and time-series charts.
